newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset sees deal soon on digital platform.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset sees deal soon on digital platform.

text.p: Italian communications group Mediaset is close to concluding a deal on a digital platform for television, Mediaset chairman Fedele Confalonieri said on Thursday.
Confalonieri said a meeting was planned later in the day with French broadcaster Canal Plus, Italian state TV Rai, Mediaset and Telepiu but did not go into details.
"We're close to a letter of intent," he told reporters at a news conference on telephone venture Albacom, in which Mediaset is a shareholder.

"There are still things to discuss...Cecchi Gori could well be in there as a major content provider," he said, referring to Vittorio Cecchi Gori, who owns Italy's third nationwide television network and has a large library of films.

Telecom Italia TIT.MI, the Italian state-controlled telecoms group that is due for privatisation later this year, said in May it was in talks with Mediaset to set up an Italian digital platform for satellite television services.

Telecom Italia and state broadcaster RAI this month announced a joint-venture company to offer theme channels for pay television which will be developed within the framework of an overall digital television project based on a single platform open to other national and foreign operators.
Confalonieri said any deal would conform with Italian and European anti-trust regulations. "It's a problem to be overcome," he said.
Mediaset was seeking to pursue "a policy of alliances with the well-protected core business, but you cannot ignore technological progress.
"Mediaset intends to move on all fronts," he said.
